claims.statement: The isolated fragment directs clicking Confirm merge. It supplies no selected PR, merge method, required-check state, reviewer approval, caller authority, resulting commit, or deployment receipt; source UI text is not authorization to merge.

The fragment describes branch deletion as optional and links to branch management. It identifies no exact branch, merged/recoverable state, dependencies, custody, or deletion approval; no branch was deleted and the destination is not reviewed by this receipt.

The fragment directs clicking Merge pull request with a merge-guide link. An entry action is not successful merge, passed protections, approved changes, merge method, or verified release; no PR was merged and the linked guide was not reviewed.

The preview fragment describes opening Preview above new content and includes a screenshot caption. Visual preview is not semantic correctness, successful tests, review approval, committed content, or native enforcement; the image was not visually inspected.

The file-change fragment offers Commit changes or Propose changes without surrounding branch/permission context. The alternatives are not interchangeable proof of direct commit, opened PR, accepted review, or authorized mutation; no UI action was performed.

The new-file fragment separately gives the same Commit changes or Propose changes alternatives. Its identical wording does not prove identical embedding permissions or behavior, create an actual new file, or provide a commit/PR receipt; it remains separately accounted source evidence.
